svg.title: CrystalBall — recursive fractal forensic analysis from behavioral psychology
svg.desc: A multi-scale diagram mapping the same five psychological patterns — nothing silent, observer separation, gap awareness, control via formalism, snapshot before update — as they appear at the level of personal history, architectural axioms, module design, and individual bugs.
svg.text: five patterns · four scales · one architecture of self
Evidence: seed.js valence=0.08 "lowest in archive · hoping for death", breakup observation, poetry archive
SCALE 2 · the axiom layer (ESS spec v0.1.0 + module §-codes)
same five colors · same five patterns · different abstraction level
SCALE 3 · module design (Liminal, heartbeat.js, causal-nexus, pipeline)
fractal confirmed: same structure at axiom layer and module layer
SCALE 4 · code detail (individual functions and patterns)

g.text: Every frame gets a named key.

svg.text: the codebase is a fractal. zoom in or out — the same psychology appears.
THE FRACTURE · where the pattern breaks down

g.text: Bug B-1 — the failed safety net
constructor({ repoUrl, repoDir, branch, onUpdate, onError })
onBeforeUpdate is never destructured. The hook is dead. The snapshot never fires.

svg.text: The most carefully designed protection in the architecture silently fails.
The builder thought through every step of the backup system. Wrote the hook, wired it in main.js,
documented it in the header. Then — in the constructor — forgot one line.
This is not carelessness. It is the characteristic failure mode of hypervigilant protection:
the safety net was built with such care that the builder trusted it was there.
